text: A system in which hedge funds submit position information to an authority that aggregates and publishes it cannot address liquidity risk, because protecting proprietary information requires so much aggregation that the resulting information loses value to market participants.
citation: Kaal and Oesterle, The History of Hedge Fund Regulation in the United States (2016). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2714974

isBasedOn.name: The History of Hedge Fund Regulation in the United States

abstract: Protection of proprietary information would require so much aggregation that the value of the information to market participants would be substantially reduced.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: applies to position reporting regimes that publish aggregated data
